title: Simulator
intro: Call a simulated provider with a test key, choose what should go wrong, then read the request, the response and every webhook. No merchant account, no real money.

guided.heading: Guided demo
guided.intro: {{count}} steps, from the token to the webhook received on your computer. Copy each command into your terminal, or play the step from this page: the response shows in the inspector.
guided.webhook: Start the overpass-cli command, then replay the step that creates the payment. The webhook reaches your server, signed with the provider's scheme.

tools.heading: Tools
tools.intro: The first guide brings the Simulator's webhooks to your computer. The second plugs your code assistant into the verified Overpass routes.

cli.heading: Receive the webhooks on your computer
cli.intro: The overpass-cli command connects to Overpass from your computer and passes each webhook to your development server. It needs no public URL, no tunnel and no open port, only Node.js 20 or later.

key.title: Create a test key
key.text: In the Test key block, create a key and copy it at once, since it is shown only once.

target.title: Choose your computer
target.text: In Where webhooks go, choose On my computer, with overpass-cli. The command then shows with your key already in.

run.title: Run the command
run.text: Put your key in place of ovp_test_... and your local server address after --forward-to, then run the command in a terminal. Leave it running, Ctrl+C stops it.

check.title: Run a payment and check
check.text: Run the simulated payment. The webhook reaches your server and Deliveries shows its status and duration. Check the signature with the webhook secret, then replay the delivery as often as you need.

mcp.heading: Plug your code assistant into the routes
mcp.intro: The Overpass MCP server gives Claude Code, Cursor or VS Code the verified routes, their state and their potholes. It is read-only and needs a personal token, which is not the test key.

token.title: Create a personal token
token.text: In the settings, Tokens tab, create a token for the MCP server use. It is shown only once.

config.title: Paste the configuration
config.text: Pick your editor, copy its configuration and put your token in place of the placeholder token.

ask.title: Ask your question
ask.text: Ask your assistant, for example, to integrate a Wave payment in your Laravel project by following the Overpass route. It finds the route, reads its state and writes the code from it.
